questions.q: In Step 1 of the lab, what action adds and positions the Caller column?
options: Opening List Layout and moving Caller into the shown-columns list, then repositioning it
Editing the sys_dictionary entry for the Incident table
Opening the condition builder and typing "Caller" as a value
Creating a brand-new field called Caller from scratch
questions.explain: List Layout controls which columns display and in what order — Caller already exists as a field; this step only changes the view.

questions.q: In Step 2, why is the AND toggle (not OR) used between the two filter conditions?
options: The lead wants only records matching both conditions — active AND assigned to Service Desk — not either alone
AND and OR produce identical results in this case
OR is not available in the condition builder
AND removes records permanently from the Incident table
questions.explain: AND narrows the list to records satisfying every stacked condition; OR would widen it to records matching just one.

questions.q: What does Group By Priority in Step 3 do to the already-filtered list?
options: Reorganizes the same filtered records into priority clusters without removing or adding any records
Removes the Step 2 filter entirely
Deletes all records that aren't Priority 1
Changes which assignment group the incidents belong to
questions.explain: Grouping is purely presentational — the filter from Step 2 stays fully in effect underneath the new clusters.

questions.q: In Step 4, what does it mean if an incident's Related Problems list shows no rows?
options: The related list is still configured to appear; its underlying query simply returned zero matching Problem records
The Related Problems related list has been removed from the form entirely
The incident table has been corrupted
The Problem table does not exist on this instance
questions.explain: A related list can be configured-but-empty — it still appears, it's just that no Problem record currently references this incident.

questions.q: What is the encoded-query equivalent of the Step 2 filter built visually in the condition builder?
options: active=true^assignment_group=Service Desk
active=true OR assignment_group=Service Desk only
priority=1^active=false
There is no encoded-query equivalent for a visually built filter
questions.explain: Every breadcrumb-based filter translates to an encoded query under the hood, with ^ representing AND.
